historical_evidence.company: Founded 2013 by Alejandro (Ale) Resnik and Owainn Robertson, offering a peer-to-peer marketplace for buying and selling used cars with white-glove inspection, financing, and delivery.
historical_evidence.market: Large addressable used-car market, but one dominated by entrenched, capital-intensive incumbents (CarMax, dealer networks) and requiring significant logistics/inspection infrastructure to operate at scale.
historical_evidence.team: Founding team had prior operating experience but no widely reported public track record of a prior successful exit as of the snapshot date.
historical_evidence.product: White-glove, high-touch used-car buying/selling experience — inspection, 24-hour test drives, financing, and delivery all bundled — a genuinely differentiated but operationally heavy product relative to a pure listings marketplace.
historical_evidence.execution: The Series C round had originally been targeted at $300M when fundraising began in May 2015; the round that actually closed in December 2015 raised $70M, led by Chinese automaker SAIC — a substantial shortfall against the original target, a real-time-visible signal of weaker-than-expected investor demand.
historical_evidence.traction: No specific unit volume, revenue, or take-rate figures were found in the contemporaneous sources reviewed for this snapshot.
historical_evidence.financial: Some mid-2015 press coverage referenced a $564M post-money valuation figure tied to the round; the size gap between the originally sought $300M and the $70M actually raised is itself a financial-health-relevant signal of reduced investor confidence relative to the company's own ambitions. ENRICHED (see benchmark_notes): an October 2015 industry analysis discloses Beepi's revenue-recognition and take-rate structure — because Beepi took ownership of each car before reselling it, the full sale price was booked as gross revenue, with a stated maximum commission/fee of 9% of the sale price representing the company's actual economic take (implying roughly $9M in 2014 net-fee revenue against a company-guided ~$350M in 2015 gross/sale-price-inclusive revenue). This is real, dated, Unit-Economics-relevant evidence — a disclosed take-rate and a gross-vs-net revenue distinction — though no cost-side figures (inspection, delivery, financing costs) were found to compute a full contribution margin.
